items.rationale: Authentication gate for article creation. Failure would allow unauthenticated article creation, leading to content pollution. JWT enforcement is standard but critical; failure mode is well-understood, reducing likelihood.
recommendations: Include negative tests for missing, expired, and malformed tokens
Verify 401 response on unauthenticated create attempts

items.rationale: Core article creation flow. Failure blocks the primary feature path. Standard CRUD operation with well-defined payload reduces likelihood of defect, but impact on user experience is major if broken.
recommendations: Verify successful creation with minimal valid payload
Verify creation with full payload including tagList
Verify author association in created response

items.rationale: Response format contract. Missing or incorrect fields break client integration but do not affect data integrity server-side. Standard REST response format reduces likelihood of deviation.
recommendations: Validate all expected fields in create response
Verify slug format, author metadata, and tagList structure

items.rationale: Input validation for required fields. The local fixture does not specify exact maximum lengths, whitespace handling, or tag validation rules, increasing likelihood of edge-case defects. Impact is moderate because invalid payloads are rejected rather than corrupting data.
recommendations: Test field omission for each required field individually
Test empty string, whitespace-only, and very long values
Verify descriptive validation error responses

items.rationale: Owner article update. Failure could allow unauthorized modification or prevent legitimate edits. Standard PUT semantics and slug-based identification reduce likelihood, but impact on data integrity is major.
recommendations: Verify owner can update each modifiable field
Verify response returns updated representation
Verify author is preserved after update

items.rationale: Partial update field preservation. The local fixture does not specify partial-update semantics; implementations may overwrite omitted fields with defaults. This ambiguity raises likelihood of behavioral variation.
recommendations: Test partial update with only one field supplied
Verify omitted fields retain original values
Review backend partial-update implementation approach

items.rationale: Security boundary for edit operations. Failure could allow unauthorized article modification. Owner-check logic is a common source of authorization bypass vulnerabilities. Critical impact due to data integrity and business rule violation.
recommendations: Test edit with missing and invalid tokens
Test edit with valid non-owner token
Verify 401/403 response and no side effects on article data

items.rationale: Owner article deletion. Standard DELETE operation with slug identification. Failure could prevent legitimate deletion or allow unauthorized deletion. Impact major due to data loss potential.
recommendations: Verify owner can delete owned article
Verify successful deletion response
Verify article is no longer retrievable after deletion

items.rationale: Post-deletion retrieval behavior. The exact not-found status and response body are not defined by the local fixture. Soft-delete implementations may behave differently from hard-delete, introducing likelihood of inconsistent behavior.
recommendations: Verify GET returns not-found after deletion
Verify response status code for deleted article retrieval

items.rationale: Security boundary for delete operations. Failure could allow unauthorized article deletion. Owner-check logic for deletion is a critical security control. Non-owner rejection is an expected ownership rule that must be verified against implementation.
recommendations: Test delete with missing and invalid tokens
Test delete with valid non-owner token
Verify 401/403 response and article remains accessible afterward

items.rationale: Update persistence observability. If title changes cause slug regeneration, subsequent reads using the old slug may fail. Caching layers could serve stale data. Impact major because lifecycle persistence is a core business rule.
recommendations: Verify updated values persist across subsequent detail reads
Verify slug regeneration behavior if title changes
Verify updatedAt or equivalent metadata is refreshed

items.rationale: Comprehensive deletion observability across detail and list endpoints. Deleted articles may remain visible due to caching, pagination inconsistencies, or filter-edge cases. Local fixture does not define list behavior after deletion, increasing likelihood of gaps.
recommendations: Verify deleted article absent from detail, global list, and filtered lists
Verify other active articles remain visible in lists
Test with author, tag, and favorited filters
